text:
Mira: Quick sync — I pushed a very small prototype for a 'graceful handback' policy visualizer in the demo console. It's meant to show the sequence when a primary model is degraded and we hand traffic to a safer variant, with auditable decision traces. Looking for feedback on triggers, metadata we must capture, and whether the simulate flow is useful. :eyes:

Jonah: Nice. Can you paste the minimal policy shape? curious how much we need to surface in the UI vs keep in the API.

Mira: Sure — here's the gist (very rough):
```json
{
  "policy_id": "handback-01",
  "triggers": ["p95_latency>800","error_rate>0.05","nan_pred"] ,
  "modes": ["transparent-redirect","degrade-to-safe","shadow-test"],
  "audit_level": "detailed",
  "fallback_model": "redwood-4-safety-quant"
}
```

Priya: A few quick thoughts: we should normalize trigger types — have latency, error, content-safety, and telemetry-integrity buckets so UI can show consistent knobs. Also add TTL and sampling rate for audits (we can't store full traces for 100% of requests).

Aisha: For the console simulate button, can we include a synthetic trace generator so customers can see the exact audit record that would be logged? even a small timeline view (decision -> matched trigger -> selected mode -> actions).

Theo: +1 on TTL and sampling. Also want a way to pin certain token fields to the audit entry (e.g., request_id, route_id, model_version, user_tier) so debug is possible without PII. We should default-strip any PII.

Sam: From product POV: show a compact safety score that aggregates active triggers and severity; let users expand to see raw triggers. For rollouts, show current rollout % and automatic rollback conditions. UX should make it obvious what will happen if a trigger fires at 2 AM.

Jonah: Operational question — who owns the schema (API team or console)? If we let console mutate the policy, we need robust validation and audit trails. I propose the API is source-of-truth and console only edits via API calls. Also require change approvals for policies impacting production routes.

Mira: Agreed — API SoT. Console can propose edits and raise a change request. We already have an approvals service; reuse that.

Priya: Telemetry: include the matched input signal (e.g., latency sample or error type), the evaluation window (5m/1h), and the policy hash/version used for the decision. That helps reproduce the exact state later.

Aisha: For storage costs: if audit_level=detailed we should default to sampled 10% unless customer explicit opts-in to 100% and has an enterprise retention plan. Also expose size estimates in console before they flip the toggle.

Theo: Security note: audit entries may contain model outputs if content-safety triggers — need redact-by-policy or tokenized storage. Tie retention to KMS keys per customer for Private deployments.

DevBot: deploy-bot: small demo UI pushed to staging (build 327). Link: https://ci/redwood/build/327 — run `npm start` locally to preview.

Sam: Can the simulate flow also show cost delta? e.g., handshake to fallback model may increase per-token cost but reduce error cost. A quick estimate would be valuable in the rollout decision screen.

Mira: We can show a delta using current per-token rates and estimated request split. UX idea: 'If this fires, expected cost +12% / latency -40%'.

Jonah: One internal-API debate: do triggers use absolute values (p95>800ms) or relative baselines (p95 > baseline * 1.5)? relative is safer across routes with different baselines. We need both. UI should allow selecting relative vs absolute.

Priya: Also add an exclude-list for routes/users to avoid noisy handbacks on internal traffic or CI. 

Aisha: Audit query UX: let users filter by policy_id, trigger_type, decision_outcome, model_version, and a free-text note. Keep query performant by indexing the common fields.

Theo: For compliance, we require immutable policy snapshots — keep a changelog per policy with who changed what and link to the approval artifact. Also add a playback mode for audits where we can re-run the decision logic against stored metrics.

Mira: Playback mode is super powerful but maybe expensive. We can make it 'simulate on demand' charged or gated. For prototype let's show it as a stub with sample logs.

Jonah: UX microcopy: avoid the word 'fallback' in customer facing text — prefer 'safe mode' or 'mitigation'. 'Fallback' is technical and can scare product folks.

Sam: Good call. 'Graceful handback' might sit weirdly in the UI; maybe 'automatic mitigation' or 'safety handoff'. We should A/B test naming.

Priya: Action items: 1) Mira to add trigger normalization and TTL/sampling fields to schema; 2) Jonah to draft API validation rules; 3) Aisha to estimate storage/costs for audit_level options; 4) Sam to mock compact safety score UI.

Mira: I'll update the demo and add a simulated trace collector. Aisha — can you drop storage numbers by EOD?

Aisha: Yep, I'll run numbers and post in this thread.

DevBot: notif: Mira added 3 comments to PR #582 (graceful-handback-console).

Jonah: One more thought — expose a lightweight 'why' explanation in the UI for each decision: e.g., "Triggered because p95=920ms over 5m > threshold 800ms". Keep it user friendly.

Mira: Exactly — transparency is key. Thanks all, I'll iterate and post an updated proto soon. :raised_hands:
